papers.title_en: VeriMath: Human-in-the-Loop Generation and Verification of Curriculum-Aligned Mathematics Assessment Items
papers.authors: Quy P. Nguyen, Duong Q. Nguyen, Dinh P. T. Nguyen, Truong-Giang T. Le, Truong A. Bui, Vi H. Vo, Quang-Thinh Bui, My-Phuong Ngo, Trong N. Do, Thao P. Le, Phuc M. Nguyen, H. Nguyen-Xuan
papers.evidence: 人在回路生成与校验课程对齐的测评题
papers.tldr: 数学试题自动生成需同时满足正确性、课程对齐、难度与可审查性，课堂落地仍难。VeriMath以标注参考题锚定考试板块和认知层级，先自动验证与引导修复，再交专家复核。基于越南12年级4555题、50项需求，两模型骨干每次运行94%需求获验证器接受草稿，严格教师就绪接受率最高56.8%。该人机回环框架能在强课程约束下产出高可审查试题草稿。
papers.abstract_en: Automatic generation of mathematics assessment items is a growing area in educational artificial intelligence, yet classroom deployment remains challenging. Generated questions must satisfy multiple constraints: mathematical correctness, curriculum alignment, appropriate cognitive difficulty, and educator reviewability. While prior work has advanced text generation, reliable assessment authoring requires granular control over localized examination formats and expert educational judgment. To address this challenge, we present VeriMath, a generalized, human-in-the-loop framework for generating rigorous, curriculum-constrained mathematics assessment drafts. Using annotated reference items, the framework anchors generation to the requested examination section and cognitive reasoning level, then applies sequential automated verification and guided repair before submitting drafts for expert review. We evaluate VeriMath through a national curriculum case study using 4,555 mathematics items from the Vietnamese Grade 12 curriculum and 50 distinct generation requirements covering multiple-choice, true/false, and short-answer formats. Across two model backbones, the framework produces verifier-accepted drafts for 94% (47/50) of requirements per run. Blind expert evaluations confirm high mathematical accuracy and curriculum alignment, with strict teacher-readiness assessments accepting up to 56.8% of generated items. Analysis of rejected drafts reveals persistent domain-agnostic challenges involving formatting, statement validity, and solution-step completeness. These findings demonstrate that VeriMath can bridge generative AI and dependable educational applications by producing highly reviewable assessment drafts within tightly constrained national curriculum frameworks.

papers.title_en: Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence with Learning Style Models: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.authors: Malithi Nawarathne, Prasanna Haddela, Nuwan Kodagoda
papers.evidence: 生成式AI结合学习风格模型支持个性化学习
papers.tldr: 生成式AI已被广泛用于教学，但如何与学习风格模型结合尚缺系统梳理。本文按PRISMA 2020流程检索Scopus、IEEE Xplore与Google Scholar（2015—2026），纳入41项研究。作者把生成式AI能力映射到VARK、Kolb、Felder-Silverman与Honey & Mumford四类风格偏好，归纳现有实现、收益与挑战。结果为大规模在线课堂的个性化、多模态实时适配提供实践路径与研究方向。
papers.abstract_en: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) has emerged as a powerful tool for transforming learning. This review examines how Generative AI can be integrated with established learning style models (VARK, Kolb, Felder-Silverman, and Honey & Mumford) to support student engagement in large online classes. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar (2015 to 2026) and included 41 studies that met the eligibility criteria. The review maps Generative AI capabilities to learning style preferences, synthesizes existing implementations, highlights benefits and challenges, and proposes pathways for future research and practice. Despite ongoing debates regarding the empirical validity of learning styles, Generative AI enables flexible, multimodal, and real-time adaptation. This study offers practical insights for educators and developers seeking to build more effective, learner centered learning systems

papers.title_en: AI-generated support, worked examples, and script-based learning in undergraduate physics: A comparative study
papers.authors: Larissa Hahn, Marie Aylin Falkenberg, Marten Hogelücht, Pascal Klein
papers.evidence: 以聊天机器人智能例题作为物理学习支持工具
papers.tldr: 生成式AI用于物理学习时，其价值可能取决于嵌入方式。本研究在本科电动力学中把九组学生整群随机分到聊天机器人智能例题、静态例题和讲义脚本三条件，比较高斯定理问题解决表现。结果显示三组概念测试与自我效能均提升但组间无显著差异，四周后静态例题优于脚本，智能例题仅可用性更高；后续作业中多数学生仍自愿选用静态例题。说明对话式呈现未带来明确额外学习收益，且好评形式未必被学生主动采用。
papers.abstract_en: Generative AI is increasingly used to support students during learning and problem solving, but its instructional value depends on how it is embedded in established learning approaches. Worked examples guide learners through the steps and reasoning of a solution; conversational AI may extend them by responding to individual questions. To isolate this added value, we compared a chatbot-delivered intelligent worked example with a matched static worked example and a lecture script. Nine recitation groups in an undergraduate electrodynamics course were cluster-randomized to the three conditions, and 86 students worked individually on a Gauss's law problem. Concept-test accuracy and self-efficacy increased significantly in all conditions, but changes did not differ significantly between groups (p=.07 for concept-test accuracy and p=.38 for self-efficacy). Four weeks later, in a reduced sample with selective participation and pre-existing group differences, students in the static worked-example condition scored higher than those in the script condition (p=.004, d=1.22), whereas the two worked-example conditions did not differ significantly. Usability, but not perceived educational value, was higher for the intelligent worked example than for the script (p=.011, d=0.88). In a subsequent homework assignment on Ampere's law with free choice of learning material (N=46), 62-71% of students in each condition reported using only the static worked example, at most 8% used exclusively the intelligent one, and 15-31% used neither. Thus, conversational delivery showed no clear additional learning benefit under the present conditions. More broadly, a learning format that is rated favorably need not be the one students voluntarily adopt.

papers.title_en: Validating LLM-Based Essay Scorers: A Comparative Analysis in Critical Online Reasoning in Medical Education
papers.authors: Daniel Baumartz, Alexander Mehler, Mevlüt Bagci, Maxim Konca
papers.evidence: 医学教育评估中基于大模型的自动作文评分
papers.tldr: 医学教育写作评估依赖昂贵的人工评分，基于LLM的自动评分器能否泛化尚不明确。研究用11个AES系统、8个LLM和668份学生回答，将2076次人工评分聚合为表现等级，并以AES特征训练线性SVM。结果显示单一分类器可跨任务和领域较准确重建人工等级，推理与内容特征最具预测力。这表明无需领域微调的通用LLM组合可近似人工评分，为自动评分的辅助或替代提供依据。
papers.abstract_en: Automated essay scorers (AES) based on large language models (LLMs) promise human-level accuracy. However, training, fine-tuning, and evaluating LLMs for specific assessment tasks is costly. In particular, the question arises whether these AES should be trained for specific domains or whether models based on generic LLMs might be sufficient. Human annotations, by contrast, are often more valid but far more expensive. This study evaluates whether ensembles of AES systems based on general-purpose LLMs can approximate human ratings of medical-education writing tasks by leveraging encoded linguistic and conceptual knowledge. The goal is to assess whether general-purpose models are applicable for assisting or potentially replacing human annotation in this domain. We experiment with 11 AES systems and 8 different LLMs and evaluate 668 student responses to 12 tasks, using \numprint{2076} evaluations by 7 human annotators. These ratings are aggregated to create consistent performance levels that can be used as target classes for classifiers trained on AES outputs. Our results show that learner classes based on human ratings can be accurately reconstructed using a linear SVM trained on a small set of AES features. A single classifier generalized well across tasks and domains, with reasoning and content features being most predictive. This suggests that out-of-the-box LLMs, even without domain-specific fine-tuning, can support automatic essay grading in medical education. While individual AES systems are insufficient alone, their combination approximates human evaluators, pointing to a reduced need for manual scoring or its supplementation with automated methods.

papers.title_en: Share your Screen and Talk to Gemini: How Young Learners Interact with Multimodal GenAI While Solving Scratch Tasks
papers.authors: Sven Jacobs, Lukas Berning, Natalie Kiesler
papers.evidence: 多模态生成式AI导师支持Scratch学习
papers.tldr: 儿童用Scratch编程时常因文字提示冗长而难以调试。研究设计可共享屏幕并进行语音对话的多模态GenAI导师，先以8个任务试运行，再让23名五、六年级学生在六节Scratch课后使用并填写问卷。结果显示导师回答可理解且可操作、未直接给出完整答案，但课堂中漏检61.5%的错误（试运行15.7%），学生提问简短且39.1%始终信任导师。研究表明可理解的人性化语音不等于正确支持，屏幕共享也不保证匹配程序状态。
papers.abstract_en: Children using Scratch to learn programming can struggle with text-heavy, lengthy explanations and hints during debugging. Verbal interactions based on screen sharing or camera data may be an interesting alternative for supporting learners. We therefore explore the quality, use, and perceptions of fifth- and sixth-graders' verbal interactions with a GenAI tutor. The goal is to investigate the quality and use of the multimodal GenAI tutor in the given context. First of all, a pilot study of eight tasks conducted without students helped inform the process of the tutor's classroom evaluation. The classroom study was realized after fifth- and sixth-graders had participated in six Scratch classroom lessons. Then 23 students were introduced to the tutor, worked on the eight tasks with the GenAI tutor, and completed a questionnaire. The analysis of the pilot and classroom study shows that the tutor's responses were intelligible and actionable, and no single turn revealed a complete solution. However, the tutor missed existing errors in 61.5% of 603 error-related classroom turns, compared to 15.7% in the pilot study. Children's voice prompts were brief and mostly responded to the tutor. Although a video had explained that responses could be incorrect, 39.1% of the children trusted the tutor's answers to always be correct. These findings have implications for educators and learners using multimodal GenAI tutors, as they need to be aware that an intelligible and human-like voice does not ensure correct support. For developers, our results suggest that screen sharing alone does not ensure responses that match the program state.

papers.title_en: Rubric-Based AES with LLM Ensembles: Scoring of Student Responses in Critical Online Reasoning Using Ensembles of LLMs
papers.authors: Daniel Baumartz, Alexander Mehler, Patrick Schrottenbacher, Leon Hammerla, Sebastian Gombert
papers.evidence: 用大模型集成对教育中学生回答进行自动作文评分
papers.tldr: 人工评分学生作答成本高且易受偏差、疲劳和漂移影响。研究采用基于评分细则的提示，在15个开放权重LLM上测试523种配置，并用集成方法评分631份德语经济学与医学教育作答。结果显示，用最佳LLM—提示配置替代一名人工评分者，可在103项标准中的91项维持或提升评分者间一致性，90项通过alt-test。表明LLM集成可辅助AES并减轻人工负担。
papers.abstract_en: Grading student responses is costly and time-consuming. Moreover, human annotators are prone to bias, fatigue, and rater drift, which further limits grading reliability. Various methods have been employed to develop automated essay scoring (AES) systems to reduce these costs and address bias-related issues. These methods range from early text-feature-based systems to current machine-learning and transformer-based models. Specifically, large language models (LLMs) offer the potential to streamline the development of AES systems. However, they are subject to well-known limitations, such as hallucinations and prompt sensitivity. This creates a need to explore the potential of a mixed-methods approach that leverages the synergies among individual LLMs through ensemble formation. We evaluate the potential of ensembles of LLMs to match human-rater agreement when grading student responses in economics and medical education across 103 criteria. We use 631 German-language responses and corresponding human ratings by 2 to 5 annotators from a previously conducted assessment. We experiment with 523 rubric-based prompt configurations across 15 open-weight LLMs and assess their consistency with human raters using Krippendorff's alpha for inter-annotator agreement (IAA) and the Alternative Annotator Test (alt-test). Our results show that replacing one human rater with the best-performing LLM--prompt configuration maintains or improves IAA for 91 of the 103 criteria and that LLMs pass the alt-test for 90 criteria. Our findings suggest that current state-of-the-art LLMs can support AES of German responses in economics and medical education, reducing human workload and enabling faster processing, while validation against human ratings remains necessary.

papers.title_en: Generative AI and the Crisis of Higher Education Assessments: Examining 'AI-Proofing' Strategies for College-Level Assessments
papers.authors: Bonam Mingole, Davis Yadav, Hui Min Lee, S. Shyam Sundar, Amulya Yadav
papers.evidence: 生成式AI对高校评价的挑战与防AI策略
papers.tldr: 高校评估正面临生成式AI带来的学术诚信危机，现有研究多局限于标准化考试或单一学科。本文收集17个学科、37位教师设计的75道真实大学课程题，其中61道被刻意设计为“LLM-proof”，用三个先进LLM在有/无补充材料下作答，并通过主题分析归纳五种防AI出题策略。结果显示最佳模型无材料约83%、有材料约85%，模型、答案格式与教师策略差异显著。研究为评估设计、诚信政策与教育场景LLM伦理提供依据。
papers.abstract_en: Higher education is confronting an academic-integrity challenge unlike any in its history. Students can now outsource homework, take-home assignments, and online examinations to large language models (LLMs) that complete them in seconds. Existing research on evaluating LLM performance on academic assessments has focused largely on standardized examinations, or on questions from college-level courses drawn from a single discipline. Far less is known about how LLMs perform on college-level assessment questions spanning multiple disciplines, that instructors have purposely designed to be AI-resistant, and about which features of such questions, if any, meaningfully constrain LLM performance. We address this gap by collecting 75 questions from authentic college coursework assessments, spanning 17 disciplines, which were contributed by 37 faculty members from ten U.S. universities and one U.K. university. Of these, 61 questions were intentionally designed by faculty members to be 'LLM-proof', while the remaining 14 questions were sourced from online courses. We then (i) evaluate three state-of-the-art LLMs' ability to correctly answer these questions with and without supplementary course materials; (ii) identify five strategies, through thematic analysis, that faculty used to make their questions harder for LLMs to solve; and (iii) test whether these strategies impact LLMs' ability to answer the questions accurately. Our experimental results show that the best-performing model scored approximately 83% without supplementary course materials and 85% with them, and we observed noteworthy differences across models, answer formats, and instructor tweaking strategies. We discuss implications for assessment design, academic-integrity policy, and the broader ethics of deploying LLMs in educational settings.

papers.title_en: EGS: A Complementary Safety Framework for Educational LLMs
papers.authors: Zexuan Fei, Zhengnan Guo, Yiming Luo, Kaiyi Huang, Aimin Zhou, Bo Jiang, Fei Tan
papers.evidence: 面向个性化教育的教育大模型安全框架
papers.tldr: 面向青少年的教育LLM存在有毒、偏见、误导及发展不适内容风险，且二元拒答难以应对模糊或好奇心驱动的提问。EGS作为轻量、模型无关的运行时护栏，通过查询审核、场景感知教学引导与回复审核，对输入按风险分级并对灰区问题做类别化教育干预。在通用与教育基准上，EGS提升了多类LLM的审核性能、拒答质量与越狱鲁棒性。该工作主张纵深防御式护栏，在增强安全的同时保留教育可用性。
papers.abstract_en: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer strong potential for personalized education, but adolescent-facing deployment raises risks of toxic, biased, misleading, or developmentally inappropriate content. We argue that educational safety should move beyond binary refusal: student queries are often ambiguous or curiosity-driven, requiring contextual guidance rather than simple blocking. We introduce the Educational Guardrail System (EGS), a lightweight, model-agnostic runtime framework that complements intrinsic alignment through query moderation, scenario-aware pedagogical guidance, and response moderation. EGS triages inputs by risk level, redirects gray-zone queries with category-specific educational interventions, and audits outputs before delivery. Experiments across general and education-specific benchmarks show that EGS improves moderation performance, refusal quality, and jailbreak robustness across diverse LLMs. These findings suggest that defense-in-depth guardrails can strengthen safety while preserving the pedagogical utility required in educational LLMs. Our code and model weights will be publicly available to support community adoption.

papers.title_en: Explain Your Code: AI-Based Examination at Class Scale
papers.authors: David Sarne, Shachar Sagi, Yossi Ben-Zion
papers.evidence: AI智能体在班级规模上考查学生对代码的理解
papers.tldr: 生成式AI削弱了代码与理解之间的关联，传统口试又难以在大规模课程中扩展。作者部署三智能体系统，由考官围绕学生自己代码的指定行进行16分钟自适应提问，另两智能体分别在不看考试或不直接看代码的情况下评分。247名学生、546场考试显示，口试分与代码质量分不相关（rho=-0.073），却与学位绩点相关（rho=0.419），人均模型花费至多1.37美元。结果表明按班级规模考查学生对自身代码的理解可行，且其评分能反映学业水平。
papers.abstract_en: Generative AI has weakened the link between working code and a student's understanding of it. Oral examination, the traditional test of that understanding, does not scale to large courses. We report the full-course deployment of a three-agent AI system that examines students on their own code. The first, the examiner, asks three questions anchored to specific lines of the submission, adapting difficulty to each answer, in a 16-minute text dialogue. The other two grade: a code reviewer that never sees the examination and a grader without direct access to the code. Authorship is assessed separately and is advisory. The system examined 247 students in an operating systems course (three exercises, 546 sittings, two examination languages). The grader's oral score was uncorrelated with the same submission's code quality score (Spearman rho = -0.073, 95% CI [-0.205, 0.063], n = 216) yet tracked degree grade point average (rho = 0.419, [0.294, 0.523], n = 214), while automated test scores sat at the ceiling. The mean of a student's two oral scores correlated with grade point average at 0.468 ([0.353, 0.568], n = 210), within the range of grades in three single-semester courses built on programming assignments. Model spend averaged at most $1.37 per sitting. In surveys, students began skeptical of the AI examination and rated it more favorably after sitting it twice. These results indicate that examining students on their own code is feasible at class scale, and that its score relates to academic standing where the code quality score does not.

papers.title_en: Lecture Board Readability as an AI-Measurable Predictor of Perceived Teaching Clarity
papers.authors: Nachshon Hirschenberger, Roni Segal, Yossi Ben-Zion
papers.evidence: 用视觉语言模型评估板书以分析教学清晰度
papers.tldr: 板书仍是数理教学核心，但其视觉可读性缺乏系统测量。研究用视觉语言模型Claude 3.5 Sonnet对56门大学物理与应用数学课程的2645张板书图像重复评分，提取可读性、组织性与视觉元素。课程层面可读性与学生感知清晰度(r=.43)和组织性(r=.46)相关，并在控制班级规模、均分和学年后仍唯一显著预测总体评教。该结果表明AI可低成本、可扩展地评估板书，为STEM教学形成性反馈提供新途径。
papers.abstract_en: Lecture boards remain central to university teaching in physics and mathematics, yet the visual quality of what instructors write has rarely been measured systematically. We examined whether a vision-language model can score board writing in a way that relates to how students perceive instruction. We analysed 2,645 board images from 56 university physics and applied mathematics courses taught by 18 lecturers, scoring each image 50 times with Claude 3.5 Sonnet on readability, organization and visual elements. Course-level readability was associated with student-rated clarity ($r$ = .43) and organization ($r$ = .46), and remained the only significant predictor of the overall survey score after controlling for class size, mean course grade and study year. These associations were robust to clustering by lecturer and remained stable when only one or two images per lecture were used. In a subsample of 100 images rated by four human raters, agreement between AI and human scores was comparable to agreement among the raters themselves for visual elements, lower for readability and weakest for organization. Student evaluations served as a benchmark of perceived clarity rather than of teaching quality as a whole. Automated analysis of board images may offer a low-cost, scalable source of formative feedback in STEM teaching.

papers.title_en: Standard-Anchored Delegation in Teachers' Use of Generative AI
papers.authors: Muhammad Saleh Farooq, Muhammad Ahmad Khan, Muhammad Jon Raza
papers.evidence: 教师将备课与批改任务委托给生成式AI
papers.tldr: 教师使用生成式AI时需决定哪些工作可交给模型，同时仍对学生负责。研究在巴基斯坦旁遮普以质性主导的混合方法访谈13名教师等，并编码12类教学任务。结果显示教师只在外部标准（如教材、评分量规）可定义正确输出且能核验时委托AI；无人接受AI拟定学习目标。作者据此提出“标准锚定委托”，建议工具先索取标准并并列展示输出，学校预留核验时间。
papers.abstract_en: Teachers who use generative AI must decide which parts of their work to hand over, while they remain accountable for what reaches students. We studied these decisions in Punjab, Pakistan, through a qualitatively driven mixed-methods study. We interviewed 13 teachers from government, private, NGO and vocational institutions, four administrators and one student, and coded each teacher's position on twelve educational tasks. Nine teachers accepted AI drafts or substantial assistance with lesson planning, but none accepted AI-drafted learning objectives, and eleven did not use AI to encourage or emotionally support students. Teachers who would accept AI marking required that the model be given a rubric or marking criteria. Building on assessment research and HCI work on verifiability, we call this pattern standard-anchored delegation: teachers handed a component of a task to AI when a standard outside the model, such as a textbook or rubric, defined a correct output and the teacher could apply that standard to the result. Having a standard was not always enough. Several government-school teachers did not use AI to mark quizzes even though the quizzes had answer keys, because they expected students to look for evidence of the teacher's effort. Checking AI output required subject knowledge and time, and private schools gave teachers more support for this than government schools did. Participants also read disclosure of AI use as a statement about whether the teacher had reviewed the work. We propose that teacher-facing AI tools ask for the relevant standard before generating and show each output beside it, and that schools account for the time that checking takes.

papers.title_en: What Do Digital Traces Predict? Task Effects, Student Differences, and Critical Online Reasoning
papers.evidence: 利用数字测评痕迹预测学生表现的学习分析
papers.tldr: 数字痕迹常被用于预测学生表现，但跨任务汇总相关可能混入任务差异而非任务内学生差异。研究分析424名大学生完成开放网络Critical Online Reasoning任务的最多527次浏览会话，在任务内与跨任务比较预测并做留一任务验证及置换控制。十二项预设主检验均不显著，浏览页面特征、查阅顺序和关系结构在留出任务上均未显示稳定增量预测力。研究提示需采用任务内评估与标准可泛化性审计，避免高估数字痕迹的预测价值。
papers.abstract_en: Digital assessment traces are increasingly used to predict student performance, often evaluated by correlating predicted and observed scores pooled across tasks. However, such correlations may reflect between-task differences rather than performance differences among students within tasks. To investigate this, we analyzed up to 527 browsing sessions from 424 university students completing open-Internet Critical Online Reasoning tasks and assessed the cross-task stability of their ratings. We evaluated the same out-of-fold predictions within and across tasks, compared three validation tiers up to leave-one-task-out, and tested incremental predictive contributions of consultation order and relational structure against matched permutation and randomization controls. None of the twelve prespecified primary tests was significant: on held-out tasks, consulted-page features showed no significant association with relative student performance, nor did observed order or relational structure add predictive value. Pooling observations across tasks substantially increased correlations, particularly for factual correctness, whose scores showed limited evidence of stable between-student differences across tasks. However, sentence embeddings yielded modest positive correlations with generic response quality on held-out tasks, without establishing added predictive value from observed order or relational structure. Our findings show that pooled predictive correlations may not reflect within-task student differences, highlighting the need for within-task evaluation and criterion generalizability audits.

papers.title_en: AI as Anchor: How Interview Sequencing Relates to the Appropriation of Synthetic Stakeholder Voices in Design Education
papers.authors: Osnat Mokryn, Oshrat Ayalon, Noga Dines, Orit Shaer
papers.evidence: 设计教育实地研究中采用大模型模拟的利益相关者
papers.tldr: 设计教育中，大语言模型正被用于模拟利益相关者，但其与真人访谈并用时如何被采纳仍不清楚。研究让8支团队（N=21）构建并互评AIS，再按“AIS优先”或“真人优先”顺序访谈，结合转录、设计物与反思分析。结果显示访谈顺序与信息解释和使用相关：AIS先访常提供宽泛框架，后访更用于验证真人经验；学生称AIS为“锚点”，其角色随位置变化。最终设计中真人来源议题更常落实为设计元素。
papers.abstract_en: Designers increasingly use large language models to simulate stakeholder conversations. Yet it remains unclear how AI-Simulated Stakeholders (AIS) are taken up when used alongside human stakeholder engagement. We report a field study in a single-institution, single-semester design course in which 8 teams (N=21) constructed, evaluated, and peer-reviewed an initial AIS. Then, the teams interviewed both AIS and human stakeholders in two sequences: AIS-first or human-first. Drawing on interview transcripts, design artifacts, course-embedded reflections, and post-course qualitative sessions, we examine exploratory patterns associated with these sequencing conditions. We find that students did not describe AIS as a neutral addition to the process. Instead, the order in which AIS and human stakeholders were formally interviewed was associated with different ways of interpreting and using information from the two sources. When the AIS interview came first, it provided a broad but often general frame that students later reconsidered through human interviews. When the AIS interview followed human engagement, AIS was more often used to revisit and validate insights already grounded in lived experience. Students described AIS as an "anchor," but its reported role varied with its position in the formal interview sequence. In the final designs, a larger proportion of prominent human-stakeholder-derived concerns than AIS-derived concerns had corresponding design elements. We contribute: characterization of AIS as a reference point whose reported role varies with its position in the formal interview sequence; exploratory empirical evidence that the implemented interview-order conditions were associated with distinct patterns of interpreting and using stakeholder input; and implications for integrating AIS into design workflows in ways that preserve direct engagement with human stakeholders

papers.title_en: WIP: Exploring Student-Created AI Agents and Instructional Videos to Foster Engagement in Computing Education
papers.authors: Lucas G. Zangari, Olufisayo Omojokun, Pedro Guillermo Feijóo-García
papers.evidence: 计算教育中学生自创对话式AI代理
papers.tldr: 在大型本科软件设计与工程课程中，提升计算机教育的学生参与度仍是教学挑战。该工作进展研究采用研究到实践取向，让学生创建教学视频教程与会话式AI代理两类作品，以促进主动学习。初步体验表明，视频带来多媒体互动但制作耗时，AI代理具新颖性和实践应用价值但工具较复杂。研究揭示学生创建作品有潜力加深课程内容投入，并支持创造力与批判性思维培养。
papers.abstract_en: This work-in-progress (WIP) research-to-practice study examines the use of student-created artifacts to promote active learning in a large undergraduate Software Design and Engineering (SWE) course. Active learning strategies have been shown to significantly enhance student engagement, comprehension, and motivation, particularly in computing education. In this work, we explore the use of student-created artifacts to foster student engagement in higher-level Computer Science (CS) courses. Specifically, we examine the experiences of undergraduate and graduate CS students who participated in the creation of two types of artifacts: instructional video tutorials and conversational AI agents. The goal being to understand how designing these artifacts could support students in applying and learning course content. Students raised valuable insights regarding both experiences. Concerning the creation of instructional videos, they appreciated the interactivity brought through multimedia to their learning experiences, although some found the strategy to be time-consuming. Similarly, when designing conversational AI agents, students enjoyed the novelty and practical application of the task, while some encountered challenges related to the complexity of tools such as \textit{Google Dialogflow ES}. We report on the potential of student-created artifacts to foster deeper engagement with course material, encouraging both creativity and critical thinking in computing education.

papers.title_en: Miscalibrated AI improves human calibration: An alignment problem for AI-assisted Decision education
papers.authors: Phillip C. Hegeman, Eeshan Hasan, Eungik Lee, Andrew Caplin, Jennifer S. Trueblood
papers.evidence: 利用AI概率输出开展AI辅助决策教育以培养校准能力
papers.tldr: AI辅助决策教育希望人通过观察模型概率来学习校准，但模型概率未必适合教学。研究以300名新手为被试，在接触94%准确率的CNN前后判断白细胞癌变概率，并比较原始保守概率、重校准概率与仅分类预测三种呈现。结果显示，只有对模型本身校准不佳的原始保守概率改善了后续人工校准，主要降低过度极端。该发现揭示AI辅助教育中的对齐难题：描述模型最优的信号未必最利于学习者。
papers.abstract_en: Using artificial intelligence (AI) well requires probabilistic thinking, and central to it is calibration: expressing certainty that matches one's actual accuracy. Calibration is a decision skill, but a notoriously difficult one to teach. Because AI systems typically generate a probability alongside every prediction, observing these probabilities may help humans learn to provide better calibrated judgments. This is one form of what we call AI-assisted decision education -- using AI to teach the judgment skills that decision-making requires -- of which learning by observation, as here, is among the simplest forms. In a preregistered experiment, novice participants (N = 300) judged the probability that images of white blood cells were cancerous, before and after exposure to a highly accurate (94%) convolutional neural network. A single model was shown in three ways, holding accuracy fixed while varying the certainty it expressed: its original probabilities, which were conservative and poorly calibrated for the model's accuracy; a recalibrated version, well calibrated for the model and correspondingly certain; or categorical predictions carrying no probability information. When later tested without the AI, only the original, conservative display improved participants' calibration. It did so by reducing over-extremity, without a condition-specific improvement in discrimination. Notably, the display that taught best was the one miscalibrated for the model. AI-assisted decision education therefore faces an alignment problem: the signal that best describes a model, need not be the signal that best supports the learner.

papers.title_en: Open Response Explorer: a Structured Collaborative Writing System for Peer-Informed Open-Response Assignments
papers.authors: Ziwei Gu, Ruixuan Chen, Elena Glassman
papers.evidence: 支持学生同伴互学的开放式回答协作写作界面
papers.tldr: 同伴互读式开放题要求学生查看、关联并学习同伴回答，有望促进协作知识建构，但自由散文缺乏结构，学生难以有效比较和梳理同伴观点。Open Response Explorer 以结构化观点单元重新组织开放回答，支持目的导向写作与同伴回答探索，并用共性角色文本片段高亮辅助比较。12人被试内实验验证了系统的有用性和易用性，显示其改变了开放回答起草与同伴探索实践。研究为以目的为中心的写作与探索设计提供启示，推动自由文本转化为结构化、可比较、可集体导航的知识制品。
papers.abstract_en: Peer-informed open-response assignments (where students view, connect, and learn from peer contributions) hold the potential to foster collaborative knowledge building, yet the unstructured nature of free-form prose prevents students from effectively comparing and making sense of peers' work. We present Open Response Explorer, an interface that recenters open responses on structured idea units through purpose-based writing and peer response exploration, augmented by common-role text segment highlighting for easy comparison. A within-subjects lab study (N=12) validated the usefulness and usability of the system, demonstrating how it shaped the open-response drafting and peer exploration practices. We discuss implications for purpose-centered authoring and exploration that transform free-form prose into structured, comparable, and collectively navigable knowledge artifacts.

papers.title_en: COSIMA Cookbook: a community-driven resource for ocean and sea-ice modelling science
papers.authors: Navid C. Constantinou, Julia Neme, Wilton Aguiar, Matthis Auger, Ashley J. Barnes, Romain Beucher, Dhruv Bhagtani, Christopher Yit Sen Bull, Hannah Dawson, Noah Day, Fabio Boeira Dias, Edward W. Doddridge, Anupiya Ellepola, Denisse Fierro-Arcos, Angus Gibson, Aidan Heerdegen, Andy McC. Hogg, Ryan M. Holmes, Maurice F. Huguenin, Wilma Huneke, Jemma Jeffree, Andrew E. Kiss, Minghang Li, Paige Martin, Josué Martínez-Moreno, Jan Jaap Meijer, Thomas Moore, Ruth Moorman, Adele K. Morrison, James Munroe, Aditya Narayanan, Micael Oliveira, Ellie Q. Y. Ong, Madelaine G. Rosevear, Christina Schmidt, Taimoor Sohail, Paul Spence, Dougal T. Squire, Anton Steketee, Charles Turner, Felipe Vilela da Silva, Marc White, Luwei Yang, Claire Yung, Jan Zika
papers.evidence: 面向海洋与海冰模式分析的开放教育资源
papers.tldr: 分析气候模型输出门槛高、隐性经验难复用。COSIMA Cookbook 以美食主题组织 Jupyter notebook，提供烹饪教程与易/进阶/区域食谱，展示 Intake、Xarray、Dask、xgcm、xESMF、eofs、Parcels 等工具。它把专家工作流打包成可复用、开放协作的教学资源，并持续通过 GitHub 与 hackathon 扩展。该资源促进 ACCESS 海洋海冰配置国际采用，支撑百余篇同行评审论文和 20 多个博士项目。
papers.abstract_en: The COSIMA Cookbook is an open educational resource for analysing ocean and sea-ice model output in Jupyter notebooks. It has been developed by the Consortium for Ocean--Sea Ice Modelling in Australia (COSIMA) as a community resource for researchers, students, and practitioners working with large gridded datasets, especially output from the ACCESS ocean--sea ice model configurations. The Cookbook is organised around a gastronomy theme: ``Cooking Tutorials'' teach generic, transferable techniques for handling model output, while "Easy Recipes", "Advanced Recipes" and "Regional Specialties" are self-contained notebooks that show how to perform concrete diagnostics and analyses. Along the way, the notebooks demonstrate open-source tools for the scientific analysis of large data, including Intake catalogues, Xarray, Dask, xgcm, xESMF, eofs, Parcels, matplotlib and Cartopy. The Cookbook addresses the steep entry cost of analysing climate model output: it packages expert, often tacit, knowledge into complete, well-documented and reusable workflows, in the same medium in which researchers actually work. It is developed openly on GitHub, is published as a documentation website, and is continuously reviewed and extended by its community through pull requests and regular hackathons. The easy access to data and analysis it provides has contributed to the international adoption of ACCESS ocean and sea-ice model configurations, and has facilitated well over 100 peer-reviewed papers and more than 20 PhD projects.
